newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks fall by lunch on economic woes.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks fall by lunch on economic woes.

text.p: Thai stocks fell by the lunchbreak on Friday as the release of economic data on Thursday sparked sales of most blue chip stocks, analysts said.
The SET index was down 3.45 points, or 0.50 percent at the lunchbreak, at 684.97. The SET 50 dropped 0.36 points, or 0.69 percent, to 51.53 in trade worth 1.13 billion baht.
"The figures show an economy in a growth recession ... although the figures weren't outside what was expected, I don't see any good news on the horizon," said an analyst at Krungthai Thanakit Plc.
Key figures released by the central bank on Thursday showed Thailand's economy slowing, analysts said, and central bank officials said the economy had not yet bottomed out.

Moody's downgrade of three Thai banks earlier on Friday, though widely anticipated, also weighed on investor sentiment as it pushed Thai Military Bank Plc and Siam City Bank Plc's subordinated debt ratings below investment grade, analysts said.
"Everyone expected them to come down but the grades really don't look good," said the Krungthai Thanakit analyst.
Shares of Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc continued their rally since they resumed trading last week. The stock gained 0.50 baht to 6.20 baht and topped the active list.
Traders said buying from the Industrial Finance Corporation of Thailand, which has agreed to run the ailing bank, may be fuelling gains.
Other large existing shareholders were also buying shares to bring down the average costs of their holdings, traders said.
Shares in the bank, which is struggling under a huge non-performing loan problem, were suspended last year at 16 baht. --James Mclean (662) 652-0642
